Nothing here needed it. ⚠ THE NAME IS THE THING TO UNDERSTAND, AND IT IS NOT A GLUTEN CLAIM. 玄蕎麦 means WHOLE, UNHULLED buckwheat — the grain milled with its husk, which is a flavour and colour claim, not a purity one. It says nothing about how much wheat flour is blended in as つなぎ, and the shop does not publish a ratio anywhere on this page. Japanese soba is normally 二八, eight parts buckwheat to two parts WHEAT, and a coeliac who reads 玄蕎麦 as "pure buckwheat" has made the single most expensive misreading available in a Japanese noodle shop. Even a confirmed 十割 kitchen dusts its boards with 打ち粉 — usually wheat flour — and boils every order of the day in the same pot of water. So every soba bowl below is flagged against, and the honest position is that this is a place a coeliac eats around rather than at. ⚠ THE SIDE DISHES ARE WHERE THE ACTUAL FOOD IS, and one of them is a genuine find: 湯葉刺し, raw yuba, is soybean skin and nothing else — fully vegan, and the only thing on this menu a vegan can order as a dish. The page also carries the practicalities: 11:00–22:00 with last orders at 21:30, 渋谷区道玄坂2-25-12 道玄坂通1階, counter 6 and tables 24, and ordering is by MOBILE QR CODE at the table rather than by speaking to anyone. ⚠ THAT LAST DETAIL MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS FOR A COELIAC: a QR ordering system has no field for "no flour in the sauce", and the person who brings the plate is not the person who could answer. If a question needs asking here, it has to be asked deliberately at the counter, not typed into the tablet. ⚠ THE DISH IS EGG OVER RICE, AND THE SAUCE IS THE WHOLE PROBLEM. An omurice itself is a thin omelette over rice — no wheat in either — which makes this one of the more promising formats in Japan until you read the sauce list. This kitchen sells the dish BY sauce, and the two house sauces are the two worst cases: ハヤシ is a demi-glace, which is by definition built on a browned FLOUR ROUX, and Japanese curry is a roux in solid brick form. The kitchen’s own sauce list — ハヤシ, トマト, キノコクリーム, 明太子, バジルトマト — is reproduced at the end of this record as options rather than dishes, because that is how the page lists them, with no prices. ⚠ AND A VEGAN CANNOT EAT HERE AT ALL. The shop is an オムライス専門店 — an omelette-rice specialist — so egg is not an ingredient in the dishes, it IS the dish. The only items on the whole board without egg are the chips.

Tabelog was not consulted: as of 2026-09-02 it returns HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare bot-challenge body, so its page is unverified rather than empty and its URL is deliberately absent from sources. 台東区西浅草2-17-11, a renovated fifty-year-old house three minutes from Tsukuba Express Asakusa; closed Thursdays; 28 seats over three floors, the ground floor standing-only and no cover charge. ⚠ THIS IS ONE OF THE BEST RECORDS IN THE TOKYO SET FOR A VEGAN, AND THE REASON IS UNUSUAL: the kitchen buys organic vegetables direct from a farm in Sanmu, Chiba, and sells them as vegetables rather than as a garnish. 季節の有機野菜のせいろ蒸し — seasonal organic vegetables STEAMED IN A BAMBOO BASKET — is a plate of vegetables and steam, and the menu then lets you choose what goes on it. That choice is printed on the page as three options with their prices, and it decides both diets at once. ⚠ SO READ THE THREE ADD-ONS CAREFULLY, BECAUSE ONE OF THEM IS THE TRAP AND IT IS THE ONE THAT COSTS MONEY. オリーブオイル and 岩塩 are listed at ¥0 — olive oil and rock salt, free, and both clear for a coeliac and a vegan. ひしお is ¥100, and the menu glosses it itself as 食べる醤油, "soy sauce you eat". 醤 is the ancestor of modern soy sauce and is fermented on a 麦麹 — a BARLEY koji — usually with wheat alongside the soybeans. It is the single wheat-bearing thing you can put on the one dish here that would otherwise be safe, it is presented as an upgrade, and 麦 is not on Japan’s statutory allergen list so nothing obliges anyone to say so. Ask for oil and salt. ⚠ AND ONE ITALIAN WORD WORTH KNOWING BEFORE ORDERING THE OTHER VEGETABLE PLATE: バーニャカウダ, bagna càuda, is not a vegetable dip in the vegan sense — the sauce is ANCHOVY, garlic and oil, and often cream. Tabelog was not consulted: as of 2026-09-02 it returns HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare bot-challenge, so its page is unverified rather than empty and its URL is absent from sources. ⚠ THIS IS THE MOST OPTION-RICH MENU IN THE TOKYO SET FOR A VEGAN, AND THAT IS PRECISELY WHY IT NEEDS CARE. Nine vegetable curries, a dal, chana masala, edamame, papad, three plain rices — no other record here offers a plant-eater this much choice. But an Indian or Nepali kitchen reaches for GHEE, CREAM, BUTTER and YOGHURT constantly and prints none of them, so almost every vegetable dish below is an "ask" rather than a "vegan". The two that are settled outright are サグパニール and バターチキン, which name their dairy in the dish. ⚠ AND THE GLUTEN PICTURE IS THE MIRROR IMAGE — unusually good, with two sharp exceptions. It states ハラールフードをご提供しています — halal food — and ベジタリアンの方にもベジタリアンメニューをご用意しております, a vegetarian menu. tokyo_rakeru_miyamasuzaka_ten_.price_note: ALMOST NO DISHES AND NO PRICES, and the reason is worth recording because the chain came closer to being useful than any other in this dataset before falling over. RAKERU is an omurice chain and it publishes two PDFs: a grand menu (Rakeru-Grand20260826.pdf, dated 2026-08-26) and — unusually — an allergen and nutrition table (Rakeru-component202608.pdf). Both were downloaded. The GRAND MENU has NO TEXT LAYER: 5.1MB of scanned image, from which exactly 15 characters extract, so not one dish or price can be read from it. The ALLERGEN TABLE does extract — 33,000 characters over six pages — and it is still unusable, for a reason worth stating precisely: the Japanese dish names do not survive extraction at all (only ASCII fragments such as "KUKU" come through), and the numeric columns drift between rows so that values land against the wrong products. Attributing an allergen to a named dish from that output would be guessing, so nothing has been taken from it. The three dishes below are the only ones named in readable text anywhere on the site, on the dining brand page, and they are printed without prices. ⚠ WHAT IS FULLY READABLE IS THE CHAIN’S OWN ALLERGEN POLICY, AND IT IS THE MOST VALUABLE THING HERE — more valuable than a dish list would have been. RAKERU declares 特定原材料及び特定原材料に準ずる28品目について、商品別にその含有を表示しております: all 28 of Japan’s designated and quasi-designated allergens, per product. That is far beyond the statutory 8 and beyond what almost any Japanese restaurant offers. And then the same page tells you what it is worth: 「厨房では調理器具や食器、使用油等に区別はないため微量混入等が発生する場合がございますので、ご理解の上ご注意下さい」 — in the kitchen there is NO SEPARATION of cooking utensils, of dishes, or of the FRYING OIL, so trace contamination can occur. It adds 「特に店舗では同時に多くの食材を扱っているため、食材別の完全な分離を保証しているものではございません」: complete separation of ingredients is not guaranteed. ⚠ THAT PAIRING IS THE LESSON, AND IT GENERALISES BEYOND THIS CHAIN. A 28-item allergen table tells a coeliac what is in the RECIPE. It says nothing about what reaches the plate from a shared fryer, and this company is honest enough to say so in writing. An allergen chart is an ingredient document, not a safety guarantee, and treating the two as the same thing is how people get hurt. The chain also warns that per-store originals, limited menus and takeaway items may be absent from the table entirely, and that the website can lag menu changes. ⚠ AND ONE MORE THING ABOUT WHEAT SPECIFICALLY: 麦 — barley — is NOT among the 28 items Japan designates, so a table this thorough still would not have flagged a barley ingredient. This record is provisional on the menu and should be re-checked if the chain ever publishes a grand menu with a text layer.

tokyo_shanghai_xiaolongbao_kit.price_note: Full menu with prices, read from the shop’s own official page and the three Gnavi menu pages it links — dim sum, à la carte, and the complete drinks list. The banquet-course and lunch pages exist and are not itemised here. Tabelog was not consulted: as of 2026-09-02 it returns HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare bot-challenge, so its page is unverified rather than empty and its URL is absent from sources. Shinjuku; the shop states the xiaolongbao are 店内手作り, folded in-house to order. ⚠ THE MOST IMPORTANT THING ON THIS RECORD IS NOT A DISH, IT IS THE WINE. 紹興酒 — Shaoxing — is brewed from glutinous rice fermented on a 麦麹, a WHEAT ferment, and it is not merely a drink here: Shaoxing is the standard deglazing wine of Chinese cooking, splashed into the wok in almost every stir-fry. That means a Chinese dish can carry wheat even when there is no soy sauce, no batter and no noodle anywhere in it — and no menu in China or Japan has ever listed it. It is why the vegetable stir-fries below are flagged "ask" rather than "gf" despite being nothing but vegetables and salt. The shop also sells it by the glass and builds its チャイナカクテル on it, so it is a drinking hazard as well as a cooking one. ⚠ THE SECOND HIDDEN WHEAT IS 豆板醤. Doubanjiang, the fermented broad-bean paste that makes 麻婆豆腐 and the 辣 dishes what they are, is traditionally fermented WITH WHEAT FLOUR. Between Shaoxing and doubanjiang, Sichuan-style Chinese food has two wheat routes that never appear in a dish name. ⚠ ON THE DUMPLINGS, ONE NUANCE WORTH GETTING RIGHT: every wrapper here is wheat, but they are not all the same wheat. 水晶海老餃子 — crystal prawn dumplings — are made in the Cantonese way from 澄粉, WHEAT STARCH, which is refined enough to be translucent and is sometimes described as gluten-free. It is not safe to treat it as such: wheat starch is a wheat product and Japan requires it declared as 小麦. Meanwhile 咸水角 and ゴマ団子 are made from GLUTINOUS RICE flour, which genuinely carries no wheat — but both are deep-fried in the same oil as the 春巻き. ⚠ FOR A VEGAN this is a hard menu with three or four real candidates: 豆苗の塩炒め is SALT-fried rather than soy-fried, 空心菜炒め, 木耳とほうれん草の和え and 豆腐の千切り和え are plant dishes in their own right. All stay "ask" because Chinese kitchens reach for chicken stock and oyster sauce as freely as for salt, and the 麻婆豆腐 here is minced pork despite being a tofu dish.

tokyo_home_s_pasta_shibuya_mai.price_note: Full grand menu with prices, tax included, read from all seven of the chain’s own menu section pages — spaghetti, pizza, cured ham, salads, antipasti, mains and desserts. The menu index carries the caveat 店舗により、一部メニューが異なります (some items differ by branch), so this is the chain grand menu rather than a Shibuya-specific board. No drinks page exists under the grand menu, so drinks are not recorded; the site’s embedded Instagram feed describes house sangrias, but a social post is not a menu and nothing has been taken from it. Tabelog was not consulted: as of 2026-09-02 it returns HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare bot-challenge, so its page is unverified rather than empty and its URL is absent from sources. ⚠ THE HEADLINE IS BLUNT: THERE IS ALMOST NOTHING HERE FOR A COELIAC. Spaghetti and pizza are the entire concept, the chain offers no gluten-free pasta or base, and the two dishes that escape the wheat — the caprese and the cured-ham platters — are cold plates. That is worth stating plainly rather than dressing up. ⚠ WHAT MAKES THIS RECORD WORTH READING IS THE SECOND INGREDIENT IN THREE DISHES, AND ONE OF THEM THE MENU ITSELF CALLS HIDDEN. バジリコとトマトのスパゲッティ is described as 大葉とローストしたクルミが隠し味 — shiso and roasted WALNUT as the 隠し味, the "secret ingredient". A tree nut, in a basil-and-tomato pasta, named nowhere in the dish title and flagged by the kitchen as something you are not supposed to notice. Anyone ordering the plainest-sounding tomato pasta on the board because it sounds safe would get walnut. ⚠ AND THE JAPANESE-ITALIAN CROSSOVER RUNS THROUGH THE WHOLE PASTA LIST: this kitchen makes SOUP spaghetti, and it builds those soups on 出汁. キノコのペペロンチーノ is described as 特製出汁でスープスパゲッティにアレンジ — a peperoncino, which in Italy is nothing but oil, garlic and chilli, rebuilt here on a house DASHI. A Japanese restaurant dashi is bonito, so that dish is fish, and dashi in Japan is very often 白だし or だし醤油, which is also wheat. アサリの塩味 uses a clam 出汁 for the same reason. The result is that even the oil-based pastas, normally a vegan’s one option in an Italian restaurant, are not safe assumptions here. ⚠ THERE IS NO VEGAN DISH ON THIS MENU AT ALL, on the published descriptions — every pasta carries cheese, cream, bacon, fish or dashi; every pizza carries mozzarella; the salads carry bacon, mayonnaise or parmesan.

The house salad, with no contents or dressing described anywhere on the page — so nothing about it is recorded here.

items.ja: 炙りベーコンのシーザーサラダ
items.note: ⚠ A CAESAR IS THREE PROBLEMS IN ONE BOWL: CROUTONS are wheat, the dressing is built on ANCHOVY and egg, and it is finished with parmesan. Add the bacon and nothing about this dish is what a salad promises.

items.ja: ざくざく食感が楽しいポテトサラダ
items.romaji: zakuzaku shokkan ga tanoshii poteto sarada
items.note: Potato bound with mayonnaise — egg. What provides the ざくざく crunch is not stated, and croutons or fried onion would be wheat.

items.ja: 特製ソースのカルパッチョ
items.note: Raw fish or beef — the page does not say which — under an undescribed house sauce.

items.ja: ハラペーニョを効かせたナチョス
items.note: ⚠ AN INTERESTING ONE ON A MENU MADE OF WHEAT: tortilla chips are CORN, not flour, so nachos are one of the few things here without wheat in the item itself. The questions are the shared fryer and whether the chips are corn or flour tortilla, neither of which is stated. Nachos are served with cheese.

items.ja: しらすとブロッコリーのガーリックマリネ
items.romaji: shirasu to burokkorī no gārikku marine
items.note: シラス are whole baby FISH; broccoli, garlic and oil otherwise. The marinade is not described.

items.ja: 生ハムとマンゴーのハニーマスカルポーネ
items.romaji: nama hamu to mangō no hanī masukarupōne
items.en: Cured ham and mango with honey mascarpone
items.note: Cured pork, mango, HONEY and mascarpone — no wheat in the ingredients, though anything served on toast would change that.

items.ja: チェリーモッツァレラと2色ミニトマトのカプレーゼ
items.romaji: cherī mottsarera to nishoku mini tomato no kapurēze
items.en: Cherry mozzarella and two-colour tomato caprese
items.note: ⚠ THE BEST COELIAC DISH ON THIS MENU, and one of only two with no wheat anywhere near it: cherry mozzarella, two kinds of small tomato, and nothing else in the description. Dairy, so not vegan.

items.ja: スイートチリ&マスカルポーネのフライドポテト
items.romaji: suīto chiri ando masukarupōne no furaido poteto
items.en: Chips with sweet chilli and mascarpone
items.note: Potato and oil carry no wheat, but the fryer is shared with whatever else this kitchen fries, and sweet chilli sauces sometimes carry wheat-derived thickeners. Mascarpone is dairy.

items.ja: ガーリックシュリンプ
items.note: Prawns in garlic and oil — no wheat in the ingredients, though garlic shrimp is often dusted in flour before frying and is usually served with bread.

items.ja: 牛100％ハンバーグ シャリアピンソース
items.price: セット 1,680円（税込） / 単品 1,480円（税込）
items.note: ⚠ "100% BEEF" DESCRIBES THE MEAT, NOT THE PATTY. A Japanese ハンバーグ is bound with PANKO breadcrumb soaked in milk, so the wheat is inside it, and the claim in the name is about the absence of pork rather than the absence of flour. A Chaliapin sauce is grated onion in a soy-based reduction — wheat again. The set adds rice and soup.

items.ja: 牛100％ハンバーグ きのこトマトソース
items.romaji: gyū hyaku-pāsento hanbāgu kinoko tomato sōsu
items.en: 100% beef hamburg with mushroom tomato sauce
items.price: セット 1,680円（税込） / 単品 1,480円（税込）
items.note: The tomato sauce is the least wheat-bearing of the three options, but the panko binder in the patty settles it regardless. Set includes rice and soup.

items.ja: 牛100％ハンバーグ デミグラスソース
items.price: セット 1,680円（税込） / 単品 1,480円（税込）
items.note: Wheat twice: PANKO in the patty and a FLOUR ROUX in the demi-glace. Set includes rice and soup.

items.ja: ブラックアンガス牛のステーキ
items.note: THE ONE HOT DISH HERE WITH A ROUTE FOR A COELIAC — steak is beef, salt and heat, with no flour in the item itself. The sauce is not described, and a Japanese steak sauce is very often soy-based, so it is worth asking for it plain or on the side.

items.ja: 炙りバスク風チーズケーキ
items.note: ⚠ WORTH ASKING ABOUT, unlike most cheesecakes: a BURNT BASQUE cheesecake has NO BISCUIT BASE at all — cheese, cream, egg, sugar and usually a spoonful of flour, which some kitchens leave out entirely. It is the only dessert on this list where the question is worth the breath. Dairy and egg either way.
A brownie is wheat flour, butter and egg. Brownies also frequently carry walnuts.
Chestnut cream over a base that is normally meringue or sponge; the cream is dairy. Chestnut is a nut, though a low-allergen one.

items.ja: ティラミス抹茶パフェ
items.note: Tiramisu is built on SAVOIARDI — sponge fingers, which are wheat — with mascarpone and egg.

items.ja: ダッチベイビーパンケーキ（ミックスベリーとチョコ）
items.romaji: Datchi Beibī pankēki (mikkusu berī to choko)
items.en: Dutch baby pancake with mixed berries and chocolate
items.note: A Dutch baby is a batter of FLOUR, egg and milk baked in a pan — wheat is the substance of it.

items.ja: アニバーサリードルチェプレート
items.note: A celebration plate, and the page states it must be RESERVED BY THE PREVIOUS DAY — which is also the one item here where a dietary request could realistically be built in, since the kitchen has a day’s notice. Its contents are not published, so nothing is recorded; the flags follow the rest of this dessert list.
